html:
SMTO-UI-0020 — This control isn't linked to a task

GUID: 47950b21-1270-45c4-8243-b4b08b43c8d7
Slug: ui-run-required
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • You used a control like Pause, Resume, Stop or a steering message, but the page didn't know which task it was for. Nothing was sent, and no task was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation that contains the task from the conversation list, and wait for its messages and status to load. The controls only know which task to act on after that task has loaded on the page.
  2. Check the task's current status first. It may already be finished, stopped or paused. A task that already ended doesn't need Pause, Resume or Stop.
  3. Use the control again from that task's own buttons. If it still fails, refresh the browser page and try once more. Refreshing reconnects the controls to the task that's showing.

What success looks like

  • The task's status changes as you asked, for example to paused or stopped, or your steering message appears.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't use the controls of a different task as a workaround.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A run control (pause, resume, cancel or inline steering) was invoked without a request ID, so no request was sent.

What this means

  • Run controls or inline steering are initialized without a request identity. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Run controls or inline steering are initialized without a request identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected run and request ID before submitting the control.

How to fix it

  • control() in native_controls.js and create() in inline_steer.js throw ui_run_required when no request ID is available (hooks.requestId and lastRequest are empty). Open the intended saved run so its controls are bound to that request ID; do not redirect the action to a different run.
  • Open the intended saved run and its current task controls before continuing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The action targets the intended existing run.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
